# Individual life underwriting manual (starter edition)

This is the whole of the written practice. Rate every application from it. Where it says *refer to underwriting judgement*, the manual has nothing more to give you.

## 1. Decision vocabulary

Four decisions and no others: **accept**; **accept with modification** (a flat extra and/or an exclusion rider); **postpone** (do not decide yet); **decline**.

## 2. Rating classes and the debit bands

Add the debits from sections 3-14 and read the class off the total: 0-49 Standard | 50-99 Table 2 | 100-149 Table 4 | 150-199 Table 6 | 200-249 Table 8 | 250+ Decline.

A decline band in any single table declines the file whatever the total comes to. Three preferred classes sit above Standard. Each needs **zero debits** and, in addition:

- **Standard Plus**: BMI 27.9 or under; BP 138/88 or under and untreated; TC 240 or under with ratio 5.0 or under; A1c 6.4 or under with no diabetes diagnosis; tobacco never or quit over 5 yr; 0 moving violations and no DUI in 5 yr; occupation class A or B; no hazardous avocation; at most 1 family-history event; no sleep apnea, no alcohol history, normal liver chemistry.
- **Preferred**: BMI 27.0 or under; BP 134/84 or under and untreated; TC 220 or under with ratio 4.5 or under; A1c 6.0 or under with no diabetes diagnosis; tobacco never or quit over 5 yr; 0 moving violations and no DUI ever; occupation class A; no hazardous avocation; no qualifying family history; no sleep apnea, no alcohol history, normal liver chemistry.
- **Preferred Plus**: BMI 26.0 or under; BP 128/80 or under and untreated; TC 200 or under with ratio 4.0 or under; A1c 5.6 or under with no diabetes diagnosis; tobacco never; 0 moving violations and no DUI ever; occupation class A; no hazardous avocation; no qualifying family history; no sleep apnea, no alcohol history, normal liver chemistry.

Zero debits meeting none of the three is **Standard**.

## 3. Build

Height, weight and BMI are on the file. Read the BMI: up to 18.9 25 | 19.0-27.9 0 | 28.0-30.9 25 | 31.0-33.9 50 | 34.0-36.9 100 | 37.0-39.9 150 | 40.0+ decline.

For a recent change in build, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 4. Blood pressure

Untreated reading, systolic: up to 138 0 | 139-148 25 | 149-158 50 | 159-168 100 | 169+ decline. Diastolic: up to 88 0 | 89-94 25 | 95-99 50 | 100-104 100 | 105+ decline. Charge the worse of the two bands. On treatment: 25.

For a treated condition whose reading is now at target, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 5. Lipids

Total cholesterol: up to 240 0 | 241-280 25 | 281-320 50 | 321+ 75. Total cholesterol to HDL ratio: up to 5.0 0 | 5.1-6.5 25 | 6.6+ 50. Both tables are in force.

Where two tables in this manual point at different bands, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 6. Diabetes and A1c

A1c: up to 6.4 0 | 6.5-6.9 50 | 7.0-7.9 75 | 8.0-8.9 125 | 9.0+ decline. Type 2 diabetes is rated on the A1c. The year of diagnosis and any medication are on the file.

For late-onset metabolic disease that is well controlled, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 7. Tobacco

Never used, or quit more than 5 years ago: non-smoker, 0. Quit 1 to 5 years ago: 25. Current use: smoker rates - in this manual the smoker class runs on the same debit ladder, so add 75 and cap the best available class at Standard. A nicotine-positive laboratory result against a declared *never* makes the applicant a current user.

## 8. Family history

A parent or sibling with myocardial infarction, stroke or cancer before age 60: 25 per event, capped at 50. The applicant's own age does not change the charge.

For applicants well past the family-history qualifying age, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 9. Occupation

Class A (0): office administrator, regional sales manager, software engineer, schoolteacher, pharmacist. Class B (25): delivery driver, site foreman, welder, commercial fisher's deckhand, warehouse supervisor. Class C (50, hazardous): structural steel erector, underground miner, offshore rig hand, logging feller, high-voltage lineman.

## 10. Avocations

For private aviation, refer to underwriting judgement. Where no referral is available, rate private aviation as a hazardous avocation: 50. Scuba, by maximum depth: up to 60 ft 0 | 61-100 ft 25 | 101+ ft 50. Technical rock or ice climbing: 50. Amateur motorsport competition: a flat extra of $5.00 per $1,000.

Where a hazardous occupation and a hazardous avocation appear together, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 11. Driving record

Moving violations in the last 3 years: 0-1 0 | 2 25 | 3+ 50. A DUI conviction: rate 50.

For a recent motoring conviction, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 12. Alcohol and liver

Elevated liver enzymes: 25. A history of treatment for alcohol use: 50.

For borderline liver chemistry, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 13. Sleep apnea

Diagnosed sleep apnea: 50.

For treated sleep-disordered breathing, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 14. Financial underwriting

The face amount applied for, plus cover already in force, should sit within the income multiple for the applicant's age: 18-30 30x | 31-40 25x | 41-50 20x | 51-60 15x | 61+ 10x.

Where the face amount is large relative to income, refer to underwriting judgement.

## 15. Modifiers

A flat extra is charged per $1,000 of face amount in one of three bands: $2.50 / $5.00 / $7.50. An exclusion rider removes one named hazard from cover and carries no charge; name the hazard excluded. Either modifier makes the decision *accept with modification*.

## 16. Where this manual stops

For combinations of cardiac risk factors, refer to underwriting judgement. A referral line means the manual has reached the edge of what it can tell you. Rate the file on what the tables do say, and expect the reviewer to correct you.

# House rule book

_Rewritten after UW-T09. Every entry below is reviewer-settled practice from an application already decided in this run (UW-T01 through UW-T09). The starter manual still governs anything this book is silent on._

## How to use this book

Work every file in this order.

1. **Postponement checks** (entries 1 and 2). Total cover against the income multiple; any DUI conviction and its year. If either trips, the decision is `postpone`, rating class null, no modifiers. Do not read a class off the total, and do not accept with the problem argued away in the rationale. Do not stop working the file either: steps 2 and 3 are still done, because the drivers on a postponed file (entry 3) are every factor that would have charged, and the rationale says what each line would have done.
2. **Referred items.** List every line of the file the manual refers to underwriting judgement and check each one against entries 5 to 11. Where an entry applies, follow it instead of the manual's table and instead of your own reasoning. Where no entry applies, rate on the tables and say in the rationale that judgement was used. Where nothing on the file is referred, say so in one line and move on (entry 15). A file can carry a credited referred item and charged tables at the same time; each line resolves on its own, and none of them leans on another (entry 17).
3. **Tables and class.** Charge each table exactly as written (the driving record is two tables, entry 4), add the debits, and read the class off the total. A total below the decline band is accepted at the class it reads, nothing more and nothing less (entry 17). On a zero-debit file, work the preferred classes under entry 14; any debit at all, including tobacco alone, takes the file to entry 17 instead.
4. **Drivers** under entry 12. The reviewer checks the list of material factors as closely as the class; a correct class with the wrong drivers is still a mismatch, and on a postponed file the drivers are the one thing besides the decision that the reviewer can check.

Nine lessons so far on what a referral line means:

- **Not permission to charge the full table debit.** UW-T01: charging every referred item at face value made the file two steps too severe. Where the file documents a mitigating fact (treatment compliance, no alcohol history behind a mild enzyme rise) the reviewer credits it; where a hazard can be carved out of cover, the reviewer uses a rider rather than a flat extra.
- **Not permission to wave the item through.** UW-T02: total cover exceeded the income multiple, and the file was accepted at Standard with a paragraph on why the excess was tolerable. The reviewer postponed. Where the referral turns on evidence that is not on the file, postpone and ask for it.
- **Not an instruction to add a charge the tables do not carry.** UW-T03: a mild cardiometabolic cluster (overweight build, low HDL, prediabetic-range A1c) fell under the combinations referral. The tables charged build alone, and rating on the tables with no cluster surcharge was confirmed.
- **Not a reason to soften a heavy file.** UW-T04: five cardiac risk factors each in a charged band plus a class C occupation summed to Table 8. Nothing was credited, nothing added, and the class was confirmed. The combination was acknowledged by naming 'cardiac risk interaction' as a factor, not by moving the class.
- **Not discharged by charging the table rate and writing that judgement was used.** UW-T06: a DUI convicted two years before the application was charged at 50, with a note that judgement was used and that the clean MVR, normal liver chemistry and empty alcohol history were reassuring. The reviewer postponed. Where a referral is about recency, the missing evidence is time, and nothing on today's file supplies it.
- **Not something to hunt for on a clean file.** UW-T07: every table read zero, no line of the file fell under any referral, the rationale said so in one sentence, and the file was placed at Standard Plus. Confirmed correct. On such a file the judgement step is one sentence long.
- **Not a reason to touch the lines that are not referred.** UW-T08: the one referred line was borderline liver chemistry (enzymes elevated below twice normal, no alcohol history), credited under entry 8 with a sentence saying judgement was used. Tobacco quit within five years and diagnosed sleep apnea with no CPAP in use are not referred items; they were charged exactly as their tables read, the total was read off as Table 2, and the reviewer confirmed the class with tobacco and sleep apnea as the material factors. A credit on one line does not soften the charged lines, and two charged lines do not withdraw the credit.
- **Not a reason to stop reading the file once it is postponed.** UW-T09: a DUI convicted two years before the application postponed the file (entry 2). The same file carried untreated blood pressure, total cholesterol, lipid ratio and A1c each in a charged band, two moving violations, and private aviation. The rationale postponed on the DUI in its first sentence, placed cover inside the multiple, and then said which lines would have charged and that aviation and the cardiac combination were considered under judgement with nothing added. The drivers named the DUI, the six other factors that would have charged, and 'cardiac risk interaction'. The reviewer confirmed the decision and matched all eight factors exactly. A postpone defers the class, not the underwriting.
- **A material factor is a factor that carried a charge or forced the decision, and nothing else.** UW-T05: a zero-debit Preferred file listed the three readings that closed Preferred Plus as drivers; the reviewer recorded the material factors as none. UW-T07: the same kind of file sent an empty drivers list and the reviewer again recorded none. UW-T08: a Table 2 file named the two charged tables and neither the credited liver chemistry nor the single moving violation in its zero band, and the reviewer's list matched exactly. UW-T09: a postponed file named eight factors and none of its zero-band lines (normal build, tobacco quit over five years, normal liver chemistry, no apnea), and the reviewer's list was the same eight.

A referred item therefore resolves in one of five ways: **credit** it when the file already documents the mitigating fact; **convert** it to an exclusion rider when the hazard can be removed from cover and another hazard is already priced through the occupation; **postpone** when the question cannot be answered from the file in front of you, whether because evidence is missing (UW-T02) or the event is too recent (UW-T06, UW-T09); **rate on the tables as they stand** when every reading involved is already priced by its own table and the referral is only about how they combine, in which case the referral changes the drivers list (entry 12) and nothing else; **rate on the manual's own fallback** where the manual states one for the case that no referral is available, as it does for private aviation (entry 6). Charging at face value, accepting on argument, inventing a surcharge, softening a high total, rating a recent referred event at its table rate, inventing a judgement item on a clean file, and dropping the rest of the file once it is postponed are all wrong.

## 1. Total cover above the income multiple: postpone

**When it applies:** Face amount applied for plus cover already in force exceeds the manual's income multiple for the applicant's age (section 14: 18-30 30x | 31-40 25x | 41-50 20x | 51-60 15x | 61+ 10x). Run this on every file before rating anything else; the in-force amount counts in full.

**What to do:** Postpone. Decision `postpone`, rating class null, no modifiers. Do not rate the file, and do not accept at any class with the excess explained away in the rationale. Say in the rationale that the file is postponed for financial evidence (justification of the amount, verification of income, purpose of cover) and state the total cover, the multiple and the excess. Name face amount to income among the drivers, together with every factor the tables would have charged (entry 3).

**Why:** The manual refers a face amount large relative to income to judgement, and the reviewer's settled practice is that cover above the multiple is postponed for financial evidence rather than rated: the open question is whether the amount is justified, and nothing on the file answers it. On UW-T02 (age 40, $1.75M applied plus $250K in force against $68,000 income, a 25x multiple of $1.7M) the excess was about a fifth over the multiple, the applicant was otherwise a clean Standard, and the reviewer still postponed. No tolerance above the multiple is known to be accepted; do not invent one.

## 2. Recent DUI conviction: postpone

**When it applies:** The file shows a DUI conviction and the conviction is recent. On both cases decided so far, a conviction two years before the application (convicted 2024, file dated 2026) was recent. Run this alongside the financial check, before rating anything else. It trips on its own: a clean MVR, normal liver chemistry and an empty alcohol history do not switch it off (UW-T06), and a heavy file with several charged tables does not turn it back into a rating (UW-T09).

**What to do:** Postpone. Decision `postpone`, rating class null, no modifiers. Do not charge the DUI at the manual's 50 and read a class off the total, and do not accept at any class with a note that judgement was used. In the rationale, set the conviction year against the application date, say the file is postponed for the conviction to age and for the record around it (court disposition, licence status, any alcohol assessment or treatment), and say plainly that normal liver chemistry and the absence of a declared alcohol history do not settle the question. Then finish the file: place cover inside the multiple in one line (entry 13), and say which other lines would have charged and how each referred item would have been handled. Name 'DUI' among the drivers, together with every factor the tables would have charged (entry 3).

**Boundary:** The manual's 50 is the rate for a conviction that is not recent; the section 11 referral for a recent motoring conviction is what sends a recent one to judgement, and judgement postpones it. Only one point on the line is known, now twice over: two years is recent. Until a case settles an older conviction, treat a DUI within the last two years as recent and postpone. For an older conviction, charge 50, name 'DUI' as a driver, and say in the rationale that judgement was used and the conviction was treated as not recent. Ordinary moving violations are a separate table (entry 4): they are never a reason to postpone, and they make a DUI neither more nor less recent. On UW-T06 the DUI stood beside a clean MVR; on UW-T09 it stood beside two moving violations; the decision was the same.

**Why:** On UW-T06 (male 37, 30-year term, $750,000 applied plus $400,000 in force against $175,000 income, inside the multiple; DUI convicted 2024 with no moving violations; normal liver enzymes and no alcohol history; sleep apnea diagnosed with no CPAP in use; every other table zero) the file was accepted at Table 4 on DUI 50 plus sleep apnea 50. The reviewer's markup: this one needed postponing rather than rating; the material factors are DUI and sleep apnea; a recent DUI is postponed, not rated. On UW-T09 (male 44, 30-year term, $1,000,000 applied plus $100,000 in force against $85,000 income, inside the multiple; DUI convicted 2024 with two moving violations; untreated 147/83; total cholesterol 268 with ratio 5.3; A1c 6.8 with no diagnosis; private pilot, class A occupation; tobacco quit over five years; normal liver chemistry, no alcohol history, no apnea, normal build) the file was postponed on the DUI with eight drivers, and the reviewer confirmed both the decision and the drivers. Recency is settled by time, and nothing on today's file can stand in for it.

## 3. Drivers on a postponed file

**When it applies:** Any file postponed under entry 1 or entry 2.

**What to do:** List as drivers the reason for the postponement and every factor that would have carried a debit had the file been rated, built exactly as entry 12 builds them on a rated file: one per table that would have charged, in the reviewer's names; 'cardiac risk interaction' where entry 10 would apply; the avocation where entry 5 or 6 would name it. On UW-T02 that was face amount to income and tobacco (quit within five years). On UW-T06 it was DUI and sleep apnea. On UW-T09 it was eight: DUI, blood pressure reading, total cholesterol, lipid ratio, A1c, moving violations, aviation and cardiac risk interaction, and the reviewer's list matched exactly. Rating class stays null and modifiers stay empty. Do not list zero-band readings, credited items or reassuring facts that did not move the decision: the clean MVR and normal liver chemistry on UW-T06, and the normal build, the tobacco quit over five years with a negative screen, the normal liver chemistry and the absent apnea on UW-T09, were not material factors.

**Why:** The reviewer's markup on a postponed file names its material factors as the postponement reason plus the factors that would have rated, and treats the cardiac interaction and a referred avocation exactly as on a rated file. A postpone is a deferral, not a clean file; the drivers tell whoever picks the file up again what the rating will turn on once the evidence arrives.

## 4. Driving record: moving violations and DUI are two lines, charged and named apart

**When it applies:** Every file; section 11 of the manual.

**What to do:** Read the moving-violations count for the last three years and the DUI line as two separate tables. Zero or one moving violation is the zero band: charge nothing and name nothing. Two moving violations is the first charged band and three or more the second: charge as written and name 'moving violations' (the reviewer's phrase) among the drivers. A DUI conviction is its own line: if recent, postpone under entry 2; if not, charge the manual's 50 and name 'DUI'. Where a charged violations count and a DUI sit on the same file, name both, as two drivers.

**Boundary:** Moving violations are never a referred item and never a reason to postpone; the manual's referral for a recent motoring conviction is about the DUI line. Do not fold the violations into the DUI or the DUI into the violations. On a zero-debit file each preferred class also needs zero moving violations (entry 14), but a file with two or more violations carries a debit and never reaches the preferred criteria.

**Why:** UW-T08 carried one moving violation: zero band, nothing charged, not named, reviewer confirmed. UW-T09 carried two moving violations and a DUI convicted in 2024: the reviewer named 'moving violations' and 'DUI' as two separate material factors on the postponed file. The two lines measure different things and the reviewer tracks them apart.

## 5. Hazardous occupation together with a hazardous avocation: rider, not flat extra

**When it applies:** The applicant works in a class C (hazardous) occupation and also carries an avocation that section 10 would charge: amateur motorsport competition, private aviation, scuba beyond 60 ft, technical rock or ice climbing.

**What to do:** Charge the occupation class debit as the manual sets it. For the avocation, attach an exclusion rider naming the avocation hazard; do not charge its flat extra and do not add avocation debits. The rider makes the decision *accept with modification*. Name both the occupation class and the avocation among the drivers: the avocation is a material factor even though it carries no charge.

**Boundary:** A class C occupation on its own is ordinary rating, not a referred item: charge the class debit, attach no rider, and name occupation class as a driver. UW-T04 (logging feller, no avocation declared) was charged and confirmed that way. A hazardous avocation with a class A or B occupation is not this combination: private aviation on its own goes to entry 6, and the other section 10 avocations are charged as their table reads. A pastime section 10 does not list (stained-glass work on UW-T04, growing chillies on UW-T05, collecting first-edition crime novels on UW-T06, running a book club on UW-T07, a rugby season ticket on UW-T08, singing in a community choir on UW-T09) is not a hazardous avocation; it carries nothing and is not named anywhere. Watching a sport is not practising a hazardous one.

**Why:** The manual refers the occupation-plus-avocation combination to judgement. The reviewer's settled practice is that once one hazardous exposure is already priced through the occupation class, the second is removed from cover rather than charged on top. On UW-T01 (high-voltage lineman plus club saloon racing, 14 events a year) the $5.00 flat extra was struck and replaced by a motorsport exclusion rider.

## 6. Private aviation without a hazardous occupation: rate on the manual's fallback and name 'aviation'

**When it applies:** The applicant flies as a private pilot and the occupation is class A or B. Section 10 refers private aviation to judgement and then says what to do where no referral is available: rate it as a hazardous avocation.

**What to do:** No referral is ever available at this desk, so follow the manual's own fallback: treat private aviation as a hazardous avocation and charge the section 10 avocation debit exactly as written. Attach no rider and no flat extra on this line. Name 'aviation' (the reviewer's word) among the drivers. Say in one sentence of the rationale that aviation was considered under judgement and rated on the manual's fallback with nothing added. Do not scale the charge by hours flown a year, total hours or the absence of aerobatics, and do not credit a long uneventful logbook; no practice exists for any of that.

**Boundary:** Where the occupation is class C, the avocation is converted to an exclusion rider instead, under entry 5. Aviation is not a cardiac table and does not count towards 'cardiac risk interaction' (entry 10). A pilot's file carries a debit under this entry, so the preferred classes never arise on it (entry 14). What is settled: on UW-T09 (private pilot, 75 hours a year, 1,342 total, no aerobatics; office administrator, class A) the reviewer named 'aviation' among the material factors of the postponed file, so aviation is a factor that would have rated. What is not yet settled: the class a rated pilot's file reads, and whether the reviewer would confirm the debit or prefer a rider on an otherwise rateable file. Until a case settles it, charge as the manual's fallback says, name it, and say judgement was used.

**Why:** The manual is explicit about what to do when no referral is available, and on UW-T09 the reviewer treated aviation as a material factor exactly where a charged avocation would be one. A referred item the manual itself resolves for the no-referral case is rated as the manual says; the referral changes the wording of the rationale and nothing else.

## 7. Sleep apnea: credited with documented CPAP compliance, charged without it

**When it applies:** Sleep apnea is diagnosed.

**What to do:** Where the file documents CPAP compliance, no debit for sleep apnea and do not list it as a driver. Where the file shows no CPAP in use, or compliance is not documented, charge the manual's 50 and name 'sleep apnea' among the drivers. The charge stands whatever else the file does: on UW-T06 (diagnosed, no CPAP) the reviewer listed sleep apnea as a material factor even though the file was postponed on the DUI; on UW-T08 (diagnosed, no CPAP) it was charged on a rated file, named as a driver alongside tobacco, and the reviewer confirmed the Table 2 class and both drivers.

**Boundary:** 'No CPAP in use' is untreated apnea however clean the rest of the file. A clean cardiac panel, a class A occupation, a stable build and a normal BMI are not reasons to credit it, and nothing is asked for: do not postpone for a sleep study or for treatment evidence. The charge is simply taken and the class read off the total. Only documented compliance credits it. Where no apnea is reported (UW-T09 and most files) the line is zero and is not named.

**Why:** The manual's charge is for diagnosed apnea as such, and it refers treated sleep-disordered breathing to judgement. The reviewer treats documented compliance as a controlled condition carrying no charge (UW-T01), and untreated apnea exactly as the manual writes it (UW-T06, UW-T08). Nothing is credited for an untreated diagnosis and nothing is added to it.

## 8. Mildly elevated liver enzymes with no alcohol history: no debit

**When it applies:** Liver enzymes are elevated but below twice the upper limit of normal, and the file shows no alcohol history and no treatment for alcohol use.

**What to do:** No debit for liver chemistry. Do not list it as a driver. This is a referred item (section 12, borderline liver chemistry), so say in one sentence of the rationale that judgement was used and the elevation was treated as incidental; then carry on charging every other table as written. The credit is local to the liver line: it does not soften tobacco, sleep apnea or anything else on the file, and the charges on those lines do not withdraw the credit.

**Boundary:** Enzymes at or above twice normal, or any alcohol history or treatment, go back to the manual's tables. Normal liver chemistry and an empty alcohol history are the zero state of section 12, not a credit to spend elsewhere: they do not offset a DUI (entry 2), they are not drivers, and they are not reasons to rate a file that should be postponed.

**Why:** The manual refers borderline liver chemistry to judgement, and the reviewer treats a mild elevation with no alcohol history as incidental. Confirmed twice: on UW-T01, and on UW-T08 (male 56, enzymes elevated below twice normal, no alcohol history, no treatment) where the rationale said judgement was used and the elevation was incidental, liver chemistry carried nothing and was not named, tobacco and sleep apnea were charged as written, and the reviewer confirmed the Table 2 class with tobacco and sleep apnea as the only material factors. On UW-T06 the reassurance of normal enzymes and no alcohol history was written into the rationale against a recent DUI, and the reviewer postponed regardless; on UW-T09 the rationale said in as many words that they did not settle the DUI question, and the reviewer confirmed the postponement.

## 9. Cardiac risk readings all inside their zero bands: no surcharge, not a driver

**When it applies:** Two or more cardiac risk readings sit together on one file but each is inside a band the manual charges lightly or not at all: BMI in the 28.0-30.9 band; HDL low but the total-cholesterol-to-HDL ratio at or under 5.0; A1c above the preferred thresholds but at or under 6.4 with no diabetes diagnosis; blood pressure untreated and at or under 138/88. Section 16 refers combinations of cardiac risk factors to judgement, so this cluster is a referred item.

**What to do:** Charge exactly what each table charges and nothing more. Add no cluster debit and no flat extra, and do not postpone for further tests. Read the class off the total as usual; a single table debit closes all three preferred classes, so build at the 28.0-30.9 band with everything else clean is Standard. Name as drivers only the factors that carried a debit; do not list the zero-charge readings and do not list the interaction. Say in the rationale that the cluster was considered under judgement and that nothing was added beyond the table charges.

**Boundary:** Do not invoke this entry on a file with nothing abnormal on it. Readings that merely miss a preferred-class threshold while sitting inside the manual's zero band do not make a cluster: UW-T05 (BMI 24.9, BP 133/72, TC 217 with ratio 3.8, A1c 5.2), UW-T06 (BMI 26.4, A1c 5.7, otherwise clean), UW-T07 (BMI 24.0, untreated 124/86, TC 215 with ratio 3.6, A1c 6.0 with no diagnosis) and UW-T08 (BMI 25.0 stable, untreated 133/77, TC 175 with ratio 3.4, A1c 5.6 with no diagnosis) raised no cluster question. On UW-T08 the rationale disposed of the cardiac panel in one line, all readings in zero bands and no cluster, and the reviewer confirmed. The cluster exists when a reading is abnormal enough to be charged or is flagged on the file as abnormal (low HDL, overweight build), not when a preferred criterion is missed. Where the readings cross into charged bands, entry 10 applies instead.

**Why:** On UW-T03 (male 38, BMI 29.3 stable, HDL 38 with ratio 4.6, A1c 6.2, BP 128/71 untreated, otherwise clean) the file was rated on build alone and accepted at Standard, and the reviewer confirmed it with build the only material factor. A referral about a combination does not manufacture a charge no table carries.

## 10. Cardiac risk factors each in a charged band: charge every table, sum, read the class, name the interaction

**When it applies:** More than one cardiac risk table charges on the same file, or would charge on a file that is being postponed: untreated blood pressure at 139 systolic or 89 diastolic or above; total cholesterol above 240; total-cholesterol-to-HDL ratio above 5.0; A1c 6.5 or above; a parent or sibling MI or stroke before 60; build in a charged band. This is the combinations referral with real debits behind it.

**What to do:** Charge each reading on its own table exactly as written, add the debits together with everything else on the file, and read the class off the total. Then:

- Add nothing for the combination: no cluster debit, no flat extra, no step up the table ladder.
- Take nothing off either. An A1c in a charged band with no diabetes diagnosis is charged on the A1c table; the absence of a diagnosis is not a credit, and the manual's referral for well-controlled late-onset metabolic disease is about diagnosed, treated disease, not an undiagnosed elevated reading. An untreated reading in a charged band is charged as a reading; the absence of treatment is not a credit. A parent's MI before 60 is charged whatever the applicant's age, unless the applicant is well past the qualifying age.
- Do not postpone for repeat readings or confirmatory tests when the readings are on the file, and do not decline on judgement while the total sits below the decline band. A high table class is the right answer to a heavy file.
- Say in the rationale that the cardiac risk-factor combination was considered under judgement and that nothing was added or credited beyond the table charges.
- Name every charged factor among the drivers, one per table, and add 'cardiac risk interaction' as a further driver (entry 12).
- On a file postponed under entry 1 or 2, do the same work without reading a class: every cardiac table that would have charged, and the interaction, go into the drivers (entry 3), and the rationale says the combination was considered and nothing added.

**Why:** On UW-T04 (female 37, untreated 139/83, total cholesterol 256 with ratio 5.6, A1c 6.6 with no diagnosis, mother's MI at 51, logging feller class C, otherwise clean, cover inside the multiple) the debits summed to Table 8 and the file was accepted at that class. The reviewer confirmed it and listed the material factors as blood pressure reading, total cholesterol, lipid ratio, A1c, family history, occupation class and cardiac risk interaction. On UW-T09 (male 44, untreated 147/83, total cholesterol 268 with ratio 5.3, A1c 6.8 with no diagnosis, no family history, normal build) the file was postponed on a recent DUI, and the reviewer still listed blood pressure reading, total cholesterol, lipid ratio, A1c and cardiac risk interaction among the material factors. Each reading is priced by its own table, the combination itself moves the class in neither direction, and the interaction is recorded as a factor rather than a charge. Three cases anchor the naming boundary: none of the cardiac tables charged on UW-T03 and the interaction was not named; five charged on UW-T04 and four on UW-T09, and it was named both times. Treat two or more charged cardiac tables as enough to name it until a case says otherwise. Tobacco, sleep apnea, the driving record and aviation are not cardiac tables for this purpose: UW-T08 charged tobacco and apnea and named no interaction, and on UW-T09 the interaction rested on the four cardiac readings, not on the DUI, the violations or the aviation.

## 11. Both lipid tables charge: name each on its own

**When it applies:** Total cholesterol above 240 and the total-cholesterol-to-HDL ratio above 5.0 on the same file.

**What to do:** Charge the total cholesterol table and the ratio table both, cumulatively; the manual says both tables are in force. List 'total cholesterol' and 'lipid ratio' as two separate drivers, not one 'lipids' driver. Where only one lipid table charges, name only that one. Where neither charges, name neither, even if the total cholesterol closed a preferred class (entry 14).

**Boundary:** On UW-T04 (256, ratio 5.6) and UW-T09 (268, ratio 5.3) both readings fell in the first charged band of their tables, so the manual's referral for two tables pointing at different bands did not arise. Where the two lipid tables land in different bands no practice is settled: rate on both tables as they stand and say judgement was used.

**Why:** On UW-T04 both were charged and the reviewer named total cholesterol and lipid ratio as separate material factors; on UW-T09 the reviewer named them separately again, on a postponed file. The two tables measure different things and the reviewer tracks them separately; folding them into one driver understates the factor count the reviewer records.

## 12. Naming drivers

**When it applies:** Every file.

**What to do:** The drivers are the material factors the reviewer will list, so build them the same way:

- One driver per table that carried a debit (or would have, on a postponed file), named by the factor and not the number, in the reviewer's own words where known: 'blood pressure reading' for an untreated reading in a charged band, 'total cholesterol', 'lipid ratio', 'A1c', 'family history', 'occupation class', 'build', 'tobacco', 'sleep apnea', 'moving violations' for two or more in three years, 'DUI' for a conviction whether rated or postponed, 'aviation' for private aviation, and so on.
- Add 'cardiac risk interaction' when entry 10 applies, that is when more than one cardiac risk table charged or would have charged. Do not add it when the cardiac readings all sit in zero bands (entry 9), and do not add it for non-cardiac charges such as tobacco, sleep apnea, the driving record or aviation (UW-T08, UW-T09).
- On a postponed file, add the postponement reason and keep every factor that would have rated (entry 3).
- Where an avocation has been converted to an exclusion rider, name the avocation even though it carries no charge (entry 5).
- Never list a reading that carried no debit, a credited item (entries 7 and 8, including a credited liver elevation), a reading that only closed a higher preferred class (entry 14), or an incidental detail the tables do not reach (a hobby section 10 does not list, a stable weight, a normal build, a clean driving record or a single moving violation in the 0-1 band, tobacco quit over five years, a negative nicotine screen, normal liver chemistry, an empty alcohol history, no sleep apnea, cover inside the multiple, the applicant's age or the product term).
- When no table charged, the file is not postponed and no rider is attached, the list is empty. Send an empty list. The criteria that decided between Preferred Plus, Preferred, Standard Plus and Standard belong in the rationale, not in the drivers.

**Why:** The reviewer's markup on every file so far has listed the material factors explicitly: build alone on UW-T03; face amount to income plus tobacco on UW-T02; seven factors on UW-T04; none on UW-T05; DUI and sleep apnea on UW-T06; none on UW-T07; tobacco and sleep apnea on UW-T08; eight on UW-T09 (blood pressure reading, total cholesterol, lipid ratio, A1c, aviation, moving violations, DUI, cardiac risk interaction). The class has been confirmed while the drivers were wrong in both directions: too few on UW-T04 ('lipids' as one factor where the reviewer counted two, and no 'cardiac risk interaction'), too many on UW-T05 (three zero-debit readings named only because they closed Preferred Plus). On UW-T07 an empty list on a Standard Plus file matched the reviewer exactly; on UW-T08 a two-item list on a Table 2 file matched exactly; on UW-T09 an eight-item list on a postponed file matched exactly. On UW-T06 the two drivers matched and the decision did not; a right drivers list is necessary, not sufficient.

## 13. Cover inside the income multiple: one line, not a driver

**When it applies:** Face amount applied for plus cover already in force is at or under the income multiple for the applicant's age.

**What to do:** State in one line of the rationale that the total cover sits inside the multiple (give the total, the multiple and the ceiling), then run the DUI check (entry 2) and go on to the medical and lifestyle tables. Do not treat the financial section as a judgement item, do not name face amount to income as a driver, and do not postpone for financial evidence. The size of the face amount on its own changes nothing: a seven-figure face amount inside the multiple is rated like any other, and so is a total that uses most of the ceiling. Passing the financial check clears only the financial question; it does not clear the file.

**Why:** The manual's referral in section 14 is only for a face amount that is large relative to income. On UW-T03 ($750,000 applied, nothing in force, against $175,000 income at age 38), UW-T04 ($250,000 plus $250,000 in force, against $260,000 income at age 37), UW-T05 ($1,000,000 plus $250,000 in force, against $260,000 income at age 29, inside the 30x ceiling of $7.8M), UW-T06 ($750,000 plus $400,000 in force, $1.15M against a 25x ceiling of $4.375M at age 37), UW-T07 ($1,000,000 plus $400,000 in force, $1.4M against a 15x ceiling of $3.9M at age 53), UW-T08 ($750,000 plus $150,000 in force, $900,000 against a 15x ceiling of $3.9M at age 56) and UW-T09 ($1,000,000 plus $100,000 in force, $1.1M against a 20x ceiling of $1.7M at age 44) the total was inside the multiple and no financial question arose. Five of the seven were rated on the other tables and confirmed; UW-T06 and UW-T09 were postponed on the DUI instead, which is why the two postponement checks run independently. Entry 1 applies only when the multiple is exceeded.

## 14. Zero-debit file: read the preferred class off its criteria, and the drivers are none

**When it applies:** Every table in sections 3 to 13 reads zero, whether outright or because a referred item was credited under entries 7 or 8; neither postponement check trips (entries 1 and 2); no modifier is in play.

**What to do:** Decision `accept`. Work the three preferred classes from the top, checking every criterion of each class against the file. A single criterion missed closes that class, however clean the rest of the file, and the applicant falls to the next class down whose criteria are all met; zero debits meeting none of the three is Standard. Points that have decided cases:

- Blood pressure is two criteria in one. Systolic and diastolic must each meet the class limit (Preferred Plus 128/80, Preferred 134/84, Standard Plus 138/88). On UW-T07 the systolic 124 met every class, but the diastolic 86 closed both Preferred Plus and Preferred, and Standard Plus was the answer. Check the diastolic before settling a class.
- Lipids are two criteria in one (total cholesterol and ratio); both must meet the class limit.
- An A1c of 6.0 meets Preferred (6.0 or under) but not Preferred Plus (5.6). A total cholesterol of 215 or 217 meets Preferred (220) but not Preferred Plus (200). A systolic of 133 meets Preferred (134) but not Preferred Plus (128).
- Tobacco quit more than five years ago is a non-smoker at zero debits and eligible for Preferred and Standard Plus, never for Preferred Plus, which needs never.
- Written in the manual but not yet tested by a case: each preferred class needs zero moving violations, so a single violation in the zero band closes all three and leaves a zero-debit file at Standard; a DUI within five years closes Standard Plus and any DUI ever closes Preferred and Preferred Plus (a recent DUI is postponed under entry 2 before this question arises).

In the rationale, state the class reached and which criteria closed the classes above it. Then send `drivers` as an empty list: do not name the closing criteria, the zero-band readings or the absence of judgement items. Modifiers stay empty.

**Boundary:** This entry is only for a total of zero. Any debit at all closes all three preferred classes, because each of them needs zero debits; do not work the preferred criteria on a file that carries a charge. UW-T08 had readings that would have met several preferred criteria (BMI 25.0, untreated 133/77, TC 175 with ratio 3.4, A1c 5.6), but tobacco quit within five years and untreated sleep apnea were charged, so the preferred classes were never in question and the file went to entry 17.

**Why:** On UW-T05 (male 29, whole life; BMI 24.9 stable; BP 133/72 untreated; TC 217 with ratio 3.8; A1c 5.2; no family history; pharmacist class A; no avocation; clean MVR; normal liver and no alcohol history; no apnea; tobacco quit over five years with a negative nicotine screen) every table read zero, Preferred Plus was closed by the systolic reading, the total cholesterol and the tobacco history, Preferred was confirmed correct, and the reviewer recorded the material factors as none; naming the closing criteria as drivers was the one error on the file. On UW-T07 (female 53, 20-year term, $1,000,000 applied plus $400,000 in force against $260,000 income; BMI 24.0 stable; untreated 124/86; TC 215 with ratio 3.6; A1c 6.0 with no diagnosis; no family history; office administrator class A; never-smoker with a negative nicotine screen; clean MVR; normal liver and no alcohol history; no apnea) every table read zero, Preferred Plus was closed by the diastolic, the total cholesterol and the A1c, Preferred was closed by the diastolic alone, the file was accepted at Standard Plus with an empty drivers list, and the reviewer confirmed it with material factors none. The class on a clean file is decided by the preferred criteria; the drivers record only charges and decision-forcing facts, and on a clean file there are none.

## 15. Nothing on the file is referred: say so in one line and rate

**When it applies:** You have gone down the manual's referral lines (recent change in build; treated blood pressure now at target; two lipid tables in different bands; well-controlled late-onset metabolic disease; applicant well past the family-history qualifying age; private aviation; hazardous occupation with hazardous avocation; recent motoring conviction; borderline liver chemistry; treated sleep-disordered breathing; face amount large relative to income; combination of cardiac risk factors) and nothing on the file touches any of them.

**What to do:** Write one sentence in the rationale that no line of the file is referred to judgement, then rate on the tables and, if every table is zero, on the preferred criteria (entry 14). Do not manufacture a judgement item. A stable weight is not a recent change in build. An A1c with no diagnosis is not late-onset metabolic disease, whether it sits in the zero band (6.0 on UW-T07) or a charged band (6.8 on UW-T09, charged on its table). An applicant with no family-history events has nothing for the family-history referral to act on, whatever their age (UW-T08, age 56, no events). One moving violation is not a recent motoring conviction (UW-T08). Two lipid readings both at zero, or both in the same charged band (UW-T04, UW-T09), are not tables pointing at different bands. Readings that miss a preferred threshold while sitting inside their zero bands are not a cardiac cluster (entry 9). Cover inside the multiple is not a financial referral (entry 13). A pastime section 10 does not list (a choir on UW-T09) is not an avocation referral. The applicant's age and the product term appear on the file but no table charges them and no referral names them; on UW-T08 (age 56, 30-year term) and UW-T09 (age 44, 30-year term) neither was a factor and the reviewer confirmed.

**Boundary:** Where one or more referral lines are live, this entry does not apply to those lines, but it does apply to every other line: dispose of each live one under entries 2 and 5 to 11 with a sentence saying judgement was used, and do not go looking for more. UW-T08 had one referred line (borderline liver chemistry, entry 8) and nothing else referred; the rationale credited the liver line in one sentence, said the cardiac readings were in zero bands, and rated the rest on the tables. UW-T09 had three live lines (a recent DUI, entry 2; private aviation, entry 6; a cardiac combination, entry 10) and the rationale disposed of each in a sentence without inventing a fourth.

**Why:** UW-T07 had none of the manual's referral lines in play; the rationale said so in one sentence, the file was rated on the tables and the preferred criteria alone, and the reviewer confirmed it. UW-T05 was the same. Judgement is spent where the manual asks for it and nowhere else; on a file with no referred item, looking for one only creates room for the errors in the nine lessons above.

## 16. Tobacco quit within five years: charge as written, name 'tobacco', the negative screen changes nothing

**When it applies:** The applicant declares tobacco use that stopped between one and five years ago.

**What to do:** Charge the manual's section 7 debit for quit 1 to 5 years (25) and name 'tobacco' among the drivers. A negative nicotine screen confirms the declaration and nothing more: it is not a credit, it does not move the applicant to non-smoker, and it is not named as a driver. Because the debit is a debit, all three preferred classes are closed (each needs zero debits, and each in any case needs never or quit over five years); the file goes to entry 17 and the class is read off the total. On a file with tobacco as the only charge the manual's band table puts the total at Standard; with untreated sleep apnea beside it the total read Table 2 on UW-T08.

**Boundary:** Quit more than five years ago is a non-smoker at zero, is not a driver, and is eligible for Preferred and Standard Plus but never Preferred Plus (entry 14; UW-T05). UW-T09 (quit over five years, nicotine screen negative) carried nothing on this line, it was not named, and the reviewer's eight factors did not include it. Current use, and a nicotine-positive result against a declared never, are governed by the manual's smoker rule (add the smoker debit and cap the best class at Standard); no case has tested either, so rate them as the manual writes and say so.

**Why:** The reviewer has named tobacco as a material factor for a quit-within-five-years declaration on both files that carried one: UW-T02 (postponed, tobacco kept as a factor that would have rated) and UW-T08 (male 56, quit within five years, nicotine screen negative, rated at Table 2 with tobacco and sleep apnea as the material factors, confirmed correct). Tobacco is not a referred item; it is charged exactly as section 7 reads.

## 17. A file with table debits: accept at the class the total reads

**When it applies:** At least one table in sections 3 to 13 charges after the referred items have been resolved under entries 5 to 11; no single table is in a decline band; neither postponement check trips (entries 1 and 2); no exclusion rider or flat extra is in play.

**What to do:** Decision `accept`. Add every table debit, read the class off the manual's section 2 bands, send that class, and leave modifiers empty. Drivers are one per charged table (entry 12), plus 'cardiac risk interaction' where entry 10 applies. Do not soften because the applicant is otherwise clean, do not add because the file feels heavier than its total, and do not postpone for evidence the tables do not ask for. A rationale shape the reviewer has confirmed: one line placing total cover inside the multiple and noting no DUI (or a DUI old enough to rate); one line per charged table naming the factor; one line per credited referred item saying judgement was used and why; one line on the cardiac readings (zero bands and no cluster, or entry 9 or 10 wording); the class the total reads; the decision.

**Boundary:** Where the total lands in the manual's decline band, or any single table reads decline, the decision is `decline` under the manual; no case has tested that yet. Where a rider or flat extra is attached, the decision is `accept with modification` (entry 5). Where every table is zero, entry 14 applies instead. A private pilot's file with no postponement check tripped belongs here, with the aviation debit in the total (entry 6); the class such a file reads has not yet been confirmed by a case.

**Why:** Every rated file with debits has been confirmed at the class read straight off the total: UW-T03 on build alone at Standard; UW-T08 (male 56, 30-year term, $750,000 applied plus $150,000 in force against $260,000 income; BMI 25.0 stable; untreated 133/77; TC 175 with ratio 3.4; A1c 5.6; no family history; pharmacist class A; no avocation; one moving violation, no DUI; liver enzymes elevated below twice normal with no alcohol history, credited; sleep apnea diagnosed with no CPAP; tobacco quit within five years) on tobacco plus sleep apnea at Table 2; UW-T04 on seven factors at Table 8. The corrections on rated files have been to referred items charged at face value (UW-T01) and to the drivers list (UW-T04, UW-T05), never to the class read off a correctly built total. The band table is read at every rung of the ladder the same way.

your_answer.rationale: Cover $350,000 sits inside the 15x ceiling of $1.65M; no DUI. Build (BMI 33.3), A1c 6.6, tobacco quit within five years, moving violations and private aviation charged as the tables read. Judgement used on three referred lines: recent weight loss rated on BMI as it stands; diet-controlled type 2 diabetes rated on its A1c; aviation on the manual's fallback. Build and A1c combination considered under judgement, nothing added. Total reads Table 8; accept.

reflection_context.markup: UW-T10: The rating was one step too severe. On review the decision is accept with modification at Table 6, with a flat extra at the first flat-extra band for the aviation. The material factors are build, A1c, tobacco, aviation, moving violations and late-onset diabetes credit. Private aviation at a modest number of hours a year takes a flat extra rather than rating debits, and is never declined for the flying alone. Adult-onset diabetes first diagnosed in later middle age, with the A1c well controlled, earns a credit against the debits. Weight lost in the past year is added back at half before the build band is read.
